title: Docs kitchen-scrap: SDK tutorial fixes & tiny sample app backlog
content:
Purpose: quick-running personal scratch for small doc fixes, triage notes, and a tiny sample-app backlog. Not polished — just capture steps, repros, and todo priorities so I can zap them during a focused 2-hour block.

Top-of-mind issues (fast wins):
- tutorial: "Getting started: Node SDK" mismatch with latest API (options object renamed). Repro: follow steps on page, run `npm i @redwood/inference@latest && node sample.js` -> error: TypeError: client.generate is not a function.
  - Quick patch: update code sample to `const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rwd-3b', input: 'hello' })` and add note about package major bump in changelog.
  - Linked PR: github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/842 (WIP) — need 2 reviewers (Jun + @lena).

- sample app: minimal chat widget (React) uses streaming example, but our stream example uses server-sent events and Next.js API route that 404s on fresh create-next-app.
  - Hypothesis: path mismatch after next 13 route changes. Quick workaround: include serverless fallback instructions and provide a Vercel-friendly example.
  - Action: add small directory `examples/chat-widget-vercel` with README and deployment note. Put in examples repo PR #119.

Backlog (tiny, prioritized):
1) Fix Node tutorial snippet (blocker for onboarding) — 1h (PR + docs update).
2) Add Vercel chat-widget example + deploy note — 3h.
3) Write 2-line note in Streaming guide about fallback to polled approach for dev environment — 30m.
4) Create a one-page ‘SDK migrating from 2024 -> 2025’ breakage checklist (breaking changes, rename mapping) — 2h.

Loose ideas / things to mention in PR descriptions:
- be explicit about version pinning in `npm i` section (e.g., `@redwood/inference@^2.0.0`) to avoid new-major surprises.
- include small troubleshooting section: "If you see X error, run npx envinfo and paste into issue" (helps reproduce).

Notes-to-self for repro steps (copy into issue templates):
- Node: v18.16.0 (tested), npm 9.5
- Steps to reproduce Node snippet failure:
  1) git clone examples/docs-node-tutorial
  2) cd node-tutorial && npm ci && node sample.js
  3) observe TypeError about client.*  -> include stack trace when filing.

Questions / unresolved:
- Should we keep both old top-level `client.generate()` pattern in a compatibility note or remove it entirely? Pros: fewer support tickets. Cons: docs clutter.
- Who owns release notes copy editing? PM or Docs? (@Jun thinks PM but needs handoff)

Local TODO checklist (me):
- [ ] Finish PR 842: update samples + add migration note (target: EOD Fri).
- [ ] Draft examples/chat-widget-vercel README + deploy steps, open PR 119 follow-up (target: next week).
- [ ] Add Troubleshooting blurb to tutorial page.
- [ ] Draft short changelog snippet for SDK release notes (2 bullet lines).

Small copy snippets to paste into docs/PRs:
- Node snippet replacement (single-line): `const resp = await client.text.generate({ model: 'rwd-3b', input: 'Write a haiku' })`
- Streaming note: "If SSE isn't supported in your host, use a short-polling fallback (example included)."

Quick dev constraints / cost notes:
- Example app should avoid paid Cedar or Dedicated-only features. Use hosted-tier demo tokens and short prompts to keep CI cheap.

Slack log pointers:
- See thread https://slack.com/archives/C02DEVX/p1647 for user reports of mismatch (includes user stack traces).

Final: keep this doc ephemeral. When PRs merged, move final checklist items into a tiny confluence page and delete this scratch.

— Aria
